$comment: Machine-readable specification of the text normalisation pipeline of docs/03-data-model.md §8,
implemented in assistant-knowledge (index side) and assistant-rag (query side).
THE ONE INVARIANT: normalisation never touches display text. It feeds chunk.normalized_text,
chunk.tsv and query-side expansion only, so an answer always quotes a document exactly as its
reviewer approved it. A normalised string that reaches a customer is a defect, not a feature.
This file is the single source for both sides. Index and query must run the SAME pipeline in the
SAME order or retrieval silently degrades: a term folded on one side and not the other simply
never matches, and the failure looks like a recall problem rather than a bug.
tools/i18n-lint checks this file against docs/03 §8, against the albaraka_fts text-search
configuration in specs/db/schema.sql, and against derja-msa.json.
Runs BEFORE language detection. Latin-script Tunisian Derja with digit substitutions
(9addéch, bch, flous) is otherwise detected as French and routed to the wrong prompt,
the wrong glossary and the wrong answer language. This is the single highest-impact
ordering decision in the pipeline.
digitSubstitutionNotes: 3 = ع and 7 = ح are near-universal across the Maghreb; 9 = ق is standard in Tunisia.
5 and 4 both appear for خ depending on the writer; 5 is far more common in Tunisia.
9' (9 followed by an apostrophe) marks ڨ, the Tunisian pronunciation of ق in words like
ڨال / ڨدام. The apostrophe must be consumed with the digit or the residue becomes a hamza.
2 = ء (hamza) and 8 = غ, 6 = ط are less frequent and lower confidence.

latinToArabic.$comment: Explicit digraphs that a character-by-character transliteration cannot infer.

arabizi_transliterate.fallbackBehaviour: An untransliterable token is left as-is and still reaches FTS; a crash here would drop the whole question.

language_detect.$comment: Answer language = question language (docs/06 §2). Detection is per message, never per conversation.

$comment: Stripping tashkīl is not cosmetic: the same word written with and without vowels must
produce the same index token, and KB authors are inconsistent about vowelisation.
Tatweel is used for visual justification in Arabic documents and carries no meaning.
Quranic annotation marks appear in copied religious text and would fragment every token.

$encoding: The database cluster must be UTF8. On SQL_ASCII the default text-search parser classifies every
non-ASCII token as `blank` — Arabic included — so to_tsvector returns nothing and the FTS channel
is dead for the language the Sharia corpus is written in. It fails silently: recall just looks
mediocre. Asserted by G4h in specs/db/tests/schema_test.sql.

fr_en.$comment: Accents removed for FTS only — 'crédit' and 'credit' must match. Display text keeps its accents.

$comment: Alef variants أ إ آ ٱ → ا, yā' ى → ي, hamza-on-waw/ya ؤ ئ → و ي, tā' marbūṭa ة → ه:
the five folds listed in docs/03 §8.
ڨ → ق is added deliberately and is NOT in the docs/03 table. Tunisian Arabic realises ق as
ڨ in everyday speech (ڨال, ڨدام, قرطاس/ڨرطاس), and KB text quoted from speech carries both
spellings. Without this fold, a Derja question and an MSA document about the same thing
never meet. It is applied on the index side as well as the query side, so nothing is lost.
پ چ ژ گ are Persian/Ottoman letters that appear in copied text and are folded to their
nearest Arabic equivalents rather than dropped.
Prefixes and suffixes are the seven + eight listed in docs/03 §8. The document lists ات
twice in its suffix set; the duplicate is removed here rather than carried forward, since
applying the same suffix strip twice would over-stem (معاملات → معام → ?).
maxStripPerSide = 1 is load-bearing. A light stemmer that strips greedily and repeatedly
collapses distinct words onto the same root and destroys precision — the failure mode is
silent, because recall looks fine while every query returns everything.
minRootLength = 3 protects the large class of triliteral Arabic roots: stripping below
three characters leaves a fragment that matches nothing usefully.

dialect_map.$comment: Derja → MSA, applied to the query only. Answers are always MSA (docs/06 §7).

glossary_expand.$comment: Synonym expansion from term_glossary, not a hand-maintained list.
$commentExpansion: Expansion is capped. An uncapped glossary expansion turns a specific question into a
bag-of-synonyms and the top-k fills with near-duplicates of the same concept.

tokenise.$comment: Digits are kept: tariff and rate questions are numeric (TARIFF_FEES is the strictest intent).

$comment: Mirrors the albaraka_fts configuration in specs/db/schema.sql, which is the executable truth.
tools/i18n-lint derives the expected mappings from schema.sql and fails if this block drifts.
Two corrections to what docs/03 §8 shows, both established empirically against PostgreSQL 18.4:
1. There is no `arabic_word` token type. The default parser emits 23 token types and arabic_word
is not among them; `ALTER TEXT SEARCH CONFIGURATION … ADD MAPPING FOR arabic_word` fails with
ERROR: token type "arabic_word" does not exist. In a UTF-8 database Arabic text is classified
as `word`, which is already mapped WITH unaccent, simple — unaccent is a no-op on Arabic and
`simple` preserves the token, so Arabic indexes correctly without any special token type.
The docs/03 snippet describes an intent, not something that can be executed.
2. Every token type the parser can emit must be mapped or its tokens are discarded in silence.
`uint` (a bare integer) was originally unmapped while `int` and `float` were mapped, so every
plain integer in the corpus was absent from the index — tariff minimums and maximums, the years
identifying loi n° 2016-48 and circulaire 2021-05, article numbers, quantities. `1500` alone
indexed to an empty tsvector. This is invisible in a smoke test and appears only as poor recall
on TARIFF_FEES, whose numeric grounding is a blocking metric at 100 % (docs/11 §3). Fixed in
schema.sql and locked by the G4 assertions.

mappings.note: `word` is what Arabic text classifies as in a UTF-8 database
uint = a bare integer (150, 1500, 2016); int only arises where a hyphen was read as a minus sign (-48). Omitting uint is what deleted every integer from the index.

intentionallyUnmapped.tag: markup: indexing '<td>' is pure noise in a corpus of normalised plain text
intentionallyUnmapped.entity: character references such as '&' would index as 'amp'
intentionallyUnmapped.protocol: 'http'/'https' — the URL itself is already indexed by url and host

knownLimitation.issue: the parser reads the hyphen in '2016-48' as a minus sign, so the article number indexes as '-48' and a query for '48' does not match it
knownLimitation.resolution: splitting hyphenated numbers is the application normaliser's job, not the text-search configuration's
knownLimitation.assertedBy: G4e in specs/db/tests/schema_test.sql — fails loudly if the behaviour changes

postgresTextSearch.stemmerIsLoadBearing: G4g proves Postgres will not match مضاربة against بالمضاربة; without the application-side light stemmer a query for a root form misses every document that writes it with a prefix

formatting.$comment: Display-side rules from docs/06 §5. Not part of normalisation; kept here so the locale contract is in one machine-readable place.

$comment: Three decimals are mandatory: Tunisian dinars divide into 1000 millimes and bank tariffs are
quoted in millimes (0.500 %, 3.000 DT). Rendering 2 decimals silently rounds a price.

numbers.$comment: ٠١٢٣٤٥٦٧٨٩ are never emitted: they break numeric grounding checks and screen readers in this stack.

dates.$comment: A Hijri date, where shown, accompanies a Gregorian one and never replaces it: contract deadlines are Gregorian.

$comment: Every mixed-direction run (a French product name inside an Arabic sentence, a figure, a
reference like [S3]) is wrapped in LRI…PDI. Without isolation a trailing parenthesis or a
citation marker jumps to the opposite end of the line and the sentence reads as corrupted.

knownDocumentDivergences.resolution: docs/06 §7 — it is the i18n authority and its mapping is the more precise one. باش marks purpose ('so that', 'in order to'); لـ is a bare preposition that also translates لـ and loses the purposive sense.
knownDocumentDivergences.action: derja-msa.json uses من أجل; docs/03 §8 to be aligned in the documentation consistency pass.

knownDocumentDivergences.topic: duplicate suffix in the Arabic stemmer list
knownDocumentDivergences.docs03: ات ون ين ان ات ها هم هن ية
knownDocumentDivergences.resolution: ات appears twice; the duplicate is dropped here. Stemming is a set operation, not a sequence, and applying the same strip twice over-stems.
knownDocumentDivergences.action: stageOrder and stem.ar.stripSuffixes carry it once.

knownDocumentDivergences.topic: the albaraka_fts DDL snippet in docs/03 §8 cannot execute
knownDocumentDivergences.docs03: ADD MAPPING FOR asciiword, word, numword WITH unaccent, simple; + ADD MAPPING FOR arabic_word WITH simple;
knownDocumentDivergences.schema: four ADD MAPPING statements covering 19 of the 23 default-parser token types; no arabic_word
knownDocumentDivergences.resolution: specs/db/schema.sql — it is executable and empirically verified. `arabic_word` does not exist (PostgreSQL 18.4: ERROR token type "arabic_word" does not exist) and Arabic needs no special token type in a UTF-8 database, because it classifies as `word`.
